elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Amended Section 6.1 still binds the Company (our client): "for twelve (12) months from the Effective Date, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products...", and HDI retains the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand. The covenant is narrowed, not deleted, so the preferred no-exclusivity position is not achieved.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 restricts participation only "with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products"; "Deerskin Products" is a defined term in Section 1.1 (men's and women's apparel and accessories from the Deerskin Catalog, expressly excluding closeout merchandise and Joan Cook Catalog products). Pre-existing language, unchanged.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Operation 1 replaced "during the term of this Agreement" with "for twelve (12) months from the Effective Date" in Section 6.1. The leading temporal phrase governs both limbs of the sentence (the Company's non-participation covenant and HDI's exclusive "Deerskin" brand right), so the restriction cannot run through the auto-renewing term under Section 4.1.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Added operative sentence: "The exclusivity provided in Section 6.1 shall terminate automatically upon HDI's failure to meet any service level or delivery date required under this Agreement." Termination is automatic (no notice/cure precondition) and the trigger is anchored to obligations "required under this Agreement" rather than a term left wholly undefined.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Same added sentence expressly covers "delivery date required under this Agreement", which captures dated obligations such as the Section 1.6 go-live deadline; release of the Section 6.1 exclusivity is automatic and does not depend on terminating the whole Agreement.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: all four fallback elements are met in operative language — defined product category (pre-existing "Deerskin Products"), a hard twelve-month cap replacing "during the term of this Agreement", and one added sentence giving automatic termination of the Section 6.1 exclusivity on HDI service-level or delivery-date failure.

Preferred is not met and is not claimed: the Company remains subject to a narrowed non-participation covenant for twelve months, so the redline sits at the fallback rather than the preferred no-exclusivity position. That is acceptable under the playbook and should be stated as the fallback in the comment, which it is.

Minimal: only the temporal trigger in Section 6.1 was edited and a single termination sentence added. Section 6.2 (closeout carve-out) and Section 6.3 (HDI's reciprocal two-year restriction, which benefits us) are untouched, no operative term is duplicated, and no requirement outside the fallback checklist (e.g. liquidated damages, audit, price protection) was introduced.

Preserves intent: Section 4.1 term and auto-renewal, termination mechanics, and all commercial provisions survive unchanged. Letting the exclusivity lapse at month twelve while the Agreement continues to renew is a permitted result, not an internal inconsistency.

Drafting hygiene only (not a defect against the checklist): the new termination sentence is rendered unnumbered immediately after Section 6.3. It should be numbered as a new Section 6.4 (or appended to Section 6.1) so it is not read as a qualifier on HDI's own restriction; it already self-identifies by referring to "the exclusivity provided in Section 6.1".

Optional hardening, also not required for completeness: because the Agreement does not use "Service Levels" as a defined term, we could tighten the trigger to "any service level, performance standard or delivery date required under this Agreement (including the Site launch date under Section 1.6)" to foreclose an HDI argument that no service levels exist.
